A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SoundnessBench. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and merged material.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-training results, verifier bug detection, ablations, synthetic-bug experiments, and experiments with multiple random seeds.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds model-training and verifier-evaluation results using MNIST images in Appendix E.

M1.justification: Both versions describe the same margin-loss and sliding-window adversarial-training framework. However, v3 Eq. (10) changes the input used in the counterexample loss while its new Algorithm 1 retains v2's expression. This leaves unclear whether a procedural change or an incomplete formula correction was intended.

E1.justification: v3 Appendix E adds training and evaluation using real, 1×28×28 MNIST images across eight model architectures. This substantially extends the represented data beyond v2's low-dimensional synthetic inputs; the original synthetic coverage remains.

E2.justification: In Tables 4 and 6, v3 replaces both Marabou versions' CNN AvgPool verification entries with unsupported markers, where v2 reported zeros. This changes their participation in those reported comparisons. The verifier families and variants otherwise remain unchanged, including in the new MNIST evaluation.

E3.justification: The new MNIST evaluation uses architecture-specific sets of 3–10 hidden-counterexample instances and equally many regular instances (Tables 12–15). The retained synthetic experiment uses ten regular instances per model. Its training budgets, attack settings, and 100-second verification timeout remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The margin-objective and window-size ablations, decision-boundary-distance analysis, synthetic-bug tests, and seed analyses are retained. v2 Tables 7–8 are merged into v3 Table 7 without changing the ablations. MNIST adds benchmark evaluation rather than a separate controlled ablation or sensitivity analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed ablation averages and the same repeated-training and verification-seed experiments. v2 Appendix B becomes v3 Appendix D without adding runs, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: v3 Tables 12–15 add extensive MNIST outcomes, including 6, 9, and 3 hidden counterexamples for CNN AvgPool, CNN Tanh, and ViT, respectively, and Marabou 2023 incorrectly verifying all three ViT instances. Retained experimental values match, apart from verification zeros replaced by unsupported markers in Tables 4 and 6.

T1.justification: v3 Eq. (10) revises the counterexample-loss definition: the correct-class logit is evaluated at x_CEX instead of v2 Eq. (9)'s x^(unv,i). Algorithm 1 does not incorporate this revision. Other mathematical changes, including splitting the attack condition into Eqs. (5)–(6), are equivalent reformulations; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: constructing hidden counterexamples to test verifier soundness and discovering bugs in three verifiers. The headline benchmark remains 26 models, 206 hidden counterexamples, and 260 regular instances.

C2.justification: v3 Section 3.5 adds the explanation that loose relaxations in larger models can mask erroneous bound computations. Appendix E documents that MNIST cases fail to expose some previously identified bugs, qualifying applicability and strengthening the rationale for small test cases. The earlier scale and attack limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds training pseudocode in Appendix A and model-size summaries in Table 8. Core hyperparameters, verifier-version references, and code/data access information remain unchanged. The additional documentation is limited by the inconsistent loss expression in Algorithm 1 and incomplete MNIST-specific settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion and citations concerning floating-point unsoundness and backdoor attacks, expands the methodological comparison with Zimmermann et al. (2022), and tabulates existing benchmarks in Appendix B. These refine the retained positioning around soundness testing rather than verifier performance.

P1.justification: v3 moves classification-specific definitions from Section 2 into Section 3.1, expands selected explanations, adds discussion and acknowledgments, and reorganizes the appendices. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a substantially different journal layout with new typography, publication headers, and an expanded author block. It merges the two ablation tables, adds the benchmark-comparison table and four MNIST tables, and introduces an algorithm display. Figure 1 is retained.

improvement.justification: The MNIST experiments provide useful evidence beyond synthetic data and reveal limits on exposing known bugs, while the expanded prior-work comparisons clarify the contribution. These gains are limited by incomplete MNIST settings and the mismatch between Eq. (10) and Algorithm 1. The revision offers a modest overall improvement while retaining the original core evidence.
